_comment: The allowlist behind risk 9: a ComfyUI custom node is arbitrary Python that
runs inside the ComfyUI process, so an imported workflow is a code-execution
vector. `builtin` is the set of stock class_types a workflow may use with no
opt-in at all. `packs` is a CATALOG, not a grant: every entry starts disabled,
and enabling one is an explicit operator act that records the exact version
`builtin` is seeded from the class_types the packaged templates already use —
verifiably correct, because those workflows run today — plus stock nodes an
author is likely to reach for when adapting one. Adding to it is a claim that
the node ships with ComfyUI itself; if that is wrong the workflow fails at
submit with ComfyUI's own validation error, which is a bad message but not a
security hole. Adding to `packs` is a supply-chain claim, which is why those
carry a repo and are inert until enabled.

packs.name: ComfyUI-Frame-Interpolation
packs.summary: RIFE/FILM frame interpolation — raises a short local clip to a higher frame rate.
